approvals.renderedFrom: The rcm s0 construction of pultec-low-boost - 27 parts, 4 cuts, 4 wire links, 5 solder bridges over 20 x 24 holes - drawn through tools/guide/render.ts by a scratch adapter and shown to him as a PNG. WHAT HE LOOKED AT WAS THE PICTURE AND NOT THESE BYTES, and that is stated here rather than collapsed into a path: the hash above is the painted candidate .vrt the materialisation path produces from the SAME construction, and the claim that the picture and the bytes are one arrangement is an agent's, evidenced by the figures agreeing (4 cuts / 4 wires / 5 bridges / 27 parts, seed 0) and recorded as a cost in docs/known-gaps.md G27.
approvals.why: The materialisation path performs no search at all (docs/known-gaps.md G22), so it records tools/stripboard/termination.ts's no-search where a search records one of Q1-Q6, and CRITERIA G2.5 is read through exitCodeFor(outcome, rule) over those six. The gate therefore had no way to admit a run that searched nothing - correctly, while nothing carried the owner's judgement, because an agent may not author the clause that would. The clause was not missing: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-pultec-five-boards-design.md names the owner's call on a render as acceptance channel 4. This entry is that call, recorded, so the gate can hear it.
ownerWords: i prefer the loose layout. It's much easier to build. I don't see the problem
if the layout is electrically correct, let's keep it. It looks fine to me
doesNotExcuse: IT DOES NOT TRAVEL TO DIFFERENT BYTES. The scope is candidateSha256 above, compared by tools/stripboard/approvals-consult.ts against the candidateSha256 run.json records - which tools/stripboard/adopt.ts has already checked against the candidate file itself. Approval of a render is approval of THAT board as rendered: a later run that places low-boost differently produces a different hash and is UNAPPROVED by this entry, with a complaint that says the board changed. A new arrangement is a new render, a new look and a new grant from him.

IT DOES NOT EXCUSE ELECTRICAL SOUNDNESS, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT CLAIM ENTIRELY. violationsOf in lib/stripboard/invariants.ts - every reference net whole in one copper component, no component carrying two nets - is not admitted here and is not admittable: his own words condition on it ("if the layout is electrically correct"), the grader refuses an unsound candidate before any outcome is reached, and make -C boards/pultec-low-boost check re-exports the netlist and checks the adopted board against it after the copy (G4). An approval is about whether a board is worth building, never about whether it is the circuit.

IT DOES NOT EXCUSE ANY OTHER CHECK THE ADOPTION GATE RUNS, AND IT ANSWERS EXACTLY ONE QUESTION: may a run that performed no search be adopted. The other nine refusals in tools/stripboard/adopt-model.ts - candidate-hash, rules-hash, span-hash, pin-pattern-hash, frozen-fixture-hash, provenance-chain, veroroute-commit, built-commit, uncommitted-layout - each still has to pass on its own, as does the candidate's own admissible outcome, which tools/stripboard/adopt-verdict.ts reads through the EXIT_CODES table before this entry is consulted at all. A board failing one of those is refused with this approval on record and unread.

IT DOES NOT MAKE THE ADMISSION INVISIBLE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE RECORD RATHER THAN A DISCLOSURE BURDEN. Every consultation answers with a verdict carrying text: the run directory holds owner-approval.txt beside run.json with his words quoted in full (tools/stripboard/materialize-approval.ts), and the adoption prints the notice naming this entry. A board admitted on his judgement rather than on a search result reads as exactly that, in the repository and in the run directory both.

IT IS NOT A STANDARD AND IT SETS NO BOUND. Nothing here says what a good board is, no figure is derived from it, and no later run may cite it as a precedent for its own numbers: his two sentences withdrew a clustering bound an agent had authored (stripboard/rules.json's kappaBench note) and they do not install a replacement. A second board needs its own render and its own look.
approvals.note: [owner] 2026-10-16, granted in chat on being shown the render of the materialised pultec-low-boost that the adoption gate had just refused, and recorded the same day. || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-10-16, and the whole of what he said in approving this board): "i prefer the loose layout. It's much easier to build. I don't see the problem" and "if the layout is electrically correct, let's keep it. It looks fine to me" - carried as he typed them, lower-case "i" and all, because a quote an agent tidies is a quote nobody can check against what was said. || THE SAME TWO SENTENCES ARE THE AUTHORITY FOR TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THAT IS NOT A DOUBLE-COUNTING: in stripboard/rules.json's kappaBench note they are why a clustering BOUND was withdrawn, and here they are why THIS BOARD may be adopted although its run searched nothing. He was shown one render and said one thing; the first consequence is about a parameter and the second about an artifact. || WHAT HE WAS SHOWN, AND THE ONE GAP IN IT: a PNG of the rcm s0 construction, drawn by a scratch adapter in a session scratchpad (docs/superpowers/specs and .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-pultec-layout-capability/task-8-report.md record that render and its two renderer gaps). The bytes this entry is scoped to are the painted candidate .vrt the materialisation path writes from the same construction, reproduced twice on 2026-10-16 at the hash above. THE LINK BETWEEN THE PICTURE AND THE BYTES IS AN AGENT'S CLAIM, not his: it rests on the figures agreeing. It is recorded as a known cost (docs/known-gaps.md G27) rather than presented as provenance he gave. || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him): WHY A REGISTRY RATHER THAN A CONSTANT OR A FLAG. A --approved flag would put the owner's judgement in an argv string, where it is unreviewable, unrecorded and available to whatever agent is in a hurry; a constant in the gate would be the gate approving its own input. This file is loaded by tools/stripboard/approvals.ts, every entry is answered as a VERDICT rather than a boolean, and tests/stripboard/approvals.test.ts fails when an entry here is consulted by nothing. || WHAT THE MECHANISM CANNOT DO, SAID PLAINLY: no file can prove he said anything. The loader refuses a record with no quote, a quote in nobody's voice and a quote that talks about him in the third person, and a fabricated plausible sentence would pass all three. What the design buys instead is that a forgery must name one board and one 64-hex hash, must live in a committed file with his name on it, and is printed into the run directory and at the adoption - so it is expensive and visible rather than impossible. That residual is G27 and is not papered over.

notes.schema: [model] Schema 1, and the one loader that reads it is tools/stripboard/approvals.ts. The shape follows stripboard/exemptions.json's convention - every entry carries its provenance, the owner's words verbatim, and an agent's rationale labelled as an agent's - for the reason that file gives: a decision with no recorded reason cannot be argued with, so the next reader re-derives it, and re-deriving a decision is how it gets quietly reversed. THE TWO FILES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED: exemptions.json excuses a MEASUREMENT of a board he built by hand from a rule the new tooling applies, and this one admits an ADOPTION of a board the tooling produced. An exemption is about how hard a board was to build; an approval is about whether a board is worth building, which is his question and nobody else's.
notes.approvals: [model] One entry per approved render. An entry's id must be unique, because it is how a notice and a run directory cite what a board was admitted on; so must its candidateSha256, because the same bytes approved twice is one decision written down twice and a consultation would answer from whichever came first. TWO ENTRIES OVER ONE BOARD ARE DELIBERATELY ALLOWED, which is where this registry differs from exemptions.json's one-entry-per-subject rule: a board is laid out again and again, so a second look at a second render is a second grant and has to be recordable. THE LOADER REFUSES BY NAME RATHER THAN DEFAULTING, AND THE DIRECTION MATTERS: the dangerous default here is "approved", and an approval that appeared out of a loader's charity would be a board written into boards/ on nobody's word.
notes.admits: [model] A termination may be admitted only if it is in ADMITTED_TERMINATIONS in tools/stripboard/approvals-model.ts, which today names no-search and nothing else. THE SIX STOPPING RULES ARE NOT IN IT AND MUST NOT BE ADDED by anybody reading this file as precedent: a run that searched is admitted or refused by exitCodeFor(outcome, rule), which is CRITERIA G2.5 as it is stated, and an approval that could admit a Q5 stop would overrule a clause CRITERIA states twice - a run that stops on Q5 is reported as a failure rather than as a result. An empty-by-default whitelist that refuses loudly is the point.
notes.candidateSha256: [model] THE SCOPE, and the field that makes this registry safe to have at all. An approval is granted over an ARTIFACT he looked at, so it is recorded against the sha256 of that artifact rather than against a board name: tools/stripboard/approvals-consult.ts compares it with the candidateSha256 run.json records, and tools/stripboard/adopt.ts has already checked that figure against the candidate file's own bytes - so the chain from these 64 characters to the file that would be copied under boards/ is closed before the entry is read. A later, different layout of the same section hashes differently and is UNAPPROVED, with a complaint that says the board changed. The cost is real and is accepted: every pipeline change that moves the produced bytes invalidates this entry and needs a fresh render and a fresh look from him, which is the correct direction - he approved a board, not a section.
notes.grantedBy: [model] "owner" is the only admitted grantor, and the whitelist of one is the invariant rather than a formality: an agent may never author the acceptance criteria for the artifact it is producing (CLAUDE.md, and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-agent-authored-boards-design.md). An exemption an agent could grant would author a criterion by subtraction; an APPROVAL an agent could grant would author it outright. Criteria reach an artifact through a rule file, a spec, or a reviewing agent that is never the one that authored it - and so do approvals.
notes.ownerWords: [model] REQUIRED, NON-EMPTY, AND VERBATIM, one utterance per entry of the list. A record that merely asserts approval - "the owner approved this on the render" - is refused by name, because his words are the evidence and a paraphrase is an agent's reconstruction of it. The list is a list rather than one string so that two sentences said separately are not concatenated by an agent into a quotation he never uttered. Three clauses in tools/stripboard/approvals-read.ts refuse the shapes a well-meaning agent actually writes: nothing quoted at all, nothing in the first or second person, and a quote that talks about him in the third person. NONE OF THE THREE PROVES HE SAID IT, which the entry's own note states: a fabricated plausible sentence passes all three, and what the design relies on instead is that the claim is scoped to one hash and visible in a committed file, a run directory and the adoption's own output.
